description: Fermium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Fm and atomic number 100. It is an actinide and the heaviest element that can be formed by neutron bombardment of lighter elements, representing the last element that can be prepared in macroscopic quantities, though pure fermium metal has not yet been prepared.
uses: Owing to the small amounts of produced fermium and all of its isotopes having relatively short half-lives, there are currently no uses for it outside basic scientific research.
characteristics: Fermium's chemistry is typical for the late actinides, with a preponderance of the +3 oxidation state but also an accessible +2 oxidation state. A total of 20 isotopes are known, with 257Fm being the longest-lived with a half-life of 100.5 days, while other isotopes have considerably shorter half-lives.
